notes: that check names `target/debug/fathom` on purpose while this clause measures the release binary: the committed completions and man pages are rendered by CI's docs leg, which builds `--all-features`, and a man page's VERSION line carries the compiled-in feature set of whatever wrote it. Regenerating them from the release binary would show a diff that is a feature list, not a documentation defect.

the release is *built and rehearsed* here, not *published*: no public remote exists, so the installer URL the docs print is still a placeholder and `dist`'s publish stage stays commented out with its reason. Owners: `reco-3gz` (announcement + install path), `reco-lnd` (the tag on a public remote), and the secrets table in `docs/concepts/release.md` §8.
`rpmbuild` is not installed here, so the `.rpm` was not written by this run; CI's packaging job builds it and reads it with `rpm -qip` (`ci.yml`, job `packaging`).

`cargo-dist` is not installed here, so `tools/rehearse_installer.py` (a localhost mirror of the release page, the shell installer, and four deliberate corruptions that must be caught) ran on CI's packaging job and not in this run. The `.deb` here is staged from the built binary, which the packager prints as a REHEARSAL line: its version is the release's, its contents are today's build.
three humans on three machines are still the missing half of `release.md` §5's ledger: a `curl | sh` that works on a runner is not one that worked on a stranger's laptop.

found here and deliberately not fixed: `packaging/man/man1/fathom.1`'s VERSION line prints the *compiled-in* feature set, so the committed page is only reproducible from the feature set that wrote it — CI's docs leg feeds it an `--all-features` build while `gen_shell_artifacts.py`'s own docstring (and ADR-002 §6.1) name the default build as the product. `check` passes on the leg that built the file and fails on a default-feature build of the same commit. The candidate fix is one line in the generator — render the declared feature set from `features.rs` instead of the compiled one — and it belongs with `e7.4`.

the criterion half of `perf_gate.py` was skipped (`--skip-benches`); CI's `perf` job runs it, and this run measured the end-to-end half, which is the half the budgets are written in — keystrokes, indexes and RSS, not microbenchmarks.
the baseline was blessed at 36b011f (2026-10-24T23:27:21Z); ADR-004 §11.10 says which numbers moved at that commit and why, and which three are breaches rather than passes.

the episode rebuild is outside that ceiling on purpose, and the report says so: at 100 000 commits it costs ~250 MiB more and is a whole-lineage derivation, not one of the four structures `reco-93w` bounded. The same O(store) term is why `warm.reindex.ms` is held and failing on a real repository (§11.9).
